I saw in my github email feed that someone left this comment earlier today and now it's gone (deleted I guess?), but I think it's worth addressing because it's probably a common question:

> Why not simply add an alias to the shell configuration file?
> `alias opencode="opencode --agent plan"`

This is what I originally tried too, but I ran into trouble because always having an `--agent=...` option messes up `opencode` subcommands, e.g. it breaks `opencode session list`:

```sh
$ opencode session list -n5
Session ID                      Title                      Updated
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ses_4372144b0ffe57Tqg4XQsHOTNC  Greeting                   3:13 PM · 1/16/2026
ses_43721e396ffeCYLkR3Kp1rkc3r  Greeting                   3:12 PM · 1/16/2026
ses_437220afaffeLpqFRU6qCi40NE  Greeting                   3:12 PM · 1/16/2026
ses_437222cdfffe75JvohDScGOEoH  Greeting                   3:12 PM · 1/16/2026
ses_4372267bcffe6j0FOgt24yy2Qy  Greeting                   3:12 PM · 1/16/2026

$ opencode --agent=plan session list -n5
opencode session list

list sessions

Options:
  -h, --help        show help                                                              [boolean]
  -v, --version     show version number                                                    [boolean]
      --print-logs  print logs to stderr                                                   [boolean]
      --log-level   log level                   [string] [choices: "DEBUG", "INFO", "WARN", "ERROR"]
```

Hi @rekram1-node @Mirrowel 👋 

Both the Anthropic API and the OpenAI API use `snake_case` for HTTP request parameters (max_tokens, budget_tokens, reasoning_effort).
  Since `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` targets the OpenAI API spec, the wire format is `snake_case`.

 > Note: Google/Gemini accepts both formats (generation_config/generationConfig, max_output_tokens/maxOutputTokens) but responds in camelCase. This is protobuf-style: accepts both on input, canonical format is camelCase.
 
 JavaScript/TypeScript uses `camelCase` by convention, so the AI SDK exposes camelCase in its TypeScript API (budgetTokens, reasoningEffort).
  Each provider SDK is responsible for converting to the correct wire format before sending the HTTP request:
  
   | Provider SDK | Input (JS/TS) | Output (HTTP) | Converts? |
  |---|---|---|---|                                                                                                                 
  | `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | `budgetTokens` | `budget_tokens` | ✅ Yes |
  | `@ai-sdk/fireworks` | `budgetTokens` | `budget_tokens` | ✅ Yes |                                                                        
  | `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` | `budgetTokens` | `budget_tokens` | ✅ Yes |
  | `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | `budgetTokens` | `budgetTokens` ❌ | Only its schema fields (`reasoningEffort` → `reasoning_effort`) | 
  
   `thinking.budgetTokens` is not in the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` schema, so it leaks onto the wire as camelCase. OpenAI-compatible proxies (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Portkey, etc.) forward it as-is, and the Anthropic API rejects it.
   
 ### Issue with PR #10109
  The "fix" was in `variants()`, which defines what options the user sees in the UI. Instead of just converting the format, it changed what gets sent — injecting `thinking.budget_tokens` for any model with "claude" in its name.                                                    
   
  This broke @Mirrowel's setup: his `reasoningEffort` variants got replaced with `thinking` params he never configured, and a new `"max"` variant appeared with `budget_tokens: 31999`. Combined with his `output: 32000`, the math gave `32000 - 31999 = 1` → `max_tokens: 1`.

The fix from #12544

  The conversion belongs in `providerOptions()` — the last function before options are passed to the SDK. If thinking.budgetTokens (camelCase)  is there and the SDK is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, rewrite the key to budget_tokens (snake_case).

  - No string matching on model names
  - No injecting values or changing available variants
  - Users who configured `reasoningEffort` get `reasoningEffort`
  - Users who configured `thinking.budgetTokens` get it correctly formatted as `budget_tokens`
